subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: As per section 2(12) of the CGST Act, the term 'associated enterprises' takes the meaning assigned to it under:

options.A: Section 92A of the Income-tax Act, 1961
options.B: Section 2(41) of the CGST Act itself, since 'document' is separately defined therein
options.C: Section 25 of the CGST Act, which deals with the concept of distinct persons
options.D: The Companies Act, 2013, under the definition of 'associate company'

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) Section 92A of the Income-tax Act, 1961

As per section 2(12) of the CGST Act, 'associated enterprises' shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in section 92A of the Income-tax Act, 1961. Broadly, an associated enterprise in relation to another enterprise means an enterprise which participates, directly or indirectly, or through one or more intermediaries, in the management or control or capital of the other enterprise.

question_html: As per section 2(93) of the CGST Act, where a consideration is payable for the supply of goods or services or both, the 'recipient' of such supply is:

options.A: The person who physically takes delivery or possession of the goods, irrespective of who is liable to pay the consideration
options.B: The person named as the buyer in the purchase order, irrespective of who actually discharges the payment obligation
options.C: The person to whom the invoice is addressed, irrespective of the terms of the underlying contract of supply
options.D: The person who is liable to pay that consideration

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) The person who is liable to pay that consideration

As per section 2(93)(a), where a consideration is payable for the supply of goods or services or both, the 'recipient' of the supply is the person who is liable to pay that consideration. Where no consideration is payable for supply of goods, the recipient is the person to whom the goods are delivered/made available; where no consideration is payable for supply of a service, the recipient is the person to whom the service is rendered.

question_html: As per the proviso to section 2(105) of the CGST Act, in relation to specified actionable claims, a person who organises or arranges, directly or indirectly, the supply of such actionable claims (including a person who owns, operates or manages a digital or electronic platform for such supply) shall be:

options.A: Deemed to be the supplier of such actionable claims, whether the actionable claims are supplied by him or through him, and irrespective of whether consideration is paid or conveyed to him or through him or placed at his disposal in any manner
options.B: Treated merely as an intermediary facilitator who bears no GST liability, since actionable claims other than specified actionable claims are outside the scope of 'goods'
options.C: Required to obtain a separate registration only if the aggregate value of actionable claims facilitated exceeds Rs. 20 lakh in a financial year
options.D: Liable to pay GST only on the commission or facilitation fee earned, and not on the value of the underlying actionable claims

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) Deemed to be the supplier of such actionable claims, whether the actionable claims are supplied by him or through him, and irrespective of whether consideration is paid or conveyed to him or through him or placed at his disposal in any manner

As per the proviso to section 2(105), a person who organises or arranges, directly or indirectly, supply of specified actionable claims, including a person who owns, operates or manages a digital or electronic platform for such supply, shall be deemed to be a supplier of such actionable claims, whether such actionable claims are supplied by him or through him, and whether consideration (including virtual digital assets) is paid or conveyed to him or through him or placed at his disposal in any manner. All provisions of the Act apply to such supplier as if he is the supplier liable to pay tax.

question_html: As per section 12(2) of the CGST Act, the time of supply of goods (under forward charge) shall be the earlier of:

options.A: The date of issue of invoice by the supplier, without regard to any other date, since receipt of payment is no longer relevant for goods under any circumstances
options.B: The date on which the purchase order is placed by the recipient or the date on which the goods are dispatched from the supplier's factory, whichever is later
options.C: The date of issue of invoice by the supplier or the last date on which he is required, under section 31, to issue the invoice with respect to the supply; or the date on which the supplier receives the payment with respect to the supply
options.D: The date on which the goods are entered in the recipient's books of account or the date on which the recipient's return is filed, whichever is earlier

answer_html:
Correct answer: (C) The date of issue of invoice by the supplier or the last date on which he is required, under section 31, to issue the invoice with respect to the supply; or the date on which the supplier receives the payment with respect to the supply

As per section 12(2), the time of supply of goods shall be the earlier of: (a) the date of issue of invoice by the supplier or the last date on which he is required under section 31 to issue the invoice with respect to the supply; or (b) the date on which the supplier receives the payment with respect to the supply. However, as discussed further, Notification No. 66/2017 CT effectively makes clause (a) the operative criterion for most registered persons.

Correct answer: (A) Only when the invoice for the supply of such goods is issued or ought to have been issued

question_html: As per the proviso to section 12(2), where the supplier of taxable goods receives an amount up to Rs. 1,000 in excess of the amount indicated in the tax invoice, the time of supply to the extent of such excess shall, at the OPTION of the supplier, be:

options.A: Mandatorily, the date on which the excess amount is received, with no option available to the supplier
options.B: The date of issue of the next periodic GST return, irrespective of when the next invoice is raised
options.C: The date on which the excess amount is refunded to the recipient, since excess payments must always be refunded
options.D: The date of issue of invoice in respect of such excess amount

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) The date of issue of invoice in respect of such excess amount

As per the proviso to section 12(2), for a payment of up to Rs. 1,000 received in excess of the value of the goods invoiced, the supplier can choose (at his option) to take the date of the invoice issued with respect to such excess amount as the time of supply of goods for that excess value. However, since GST on supply of goods is payable only on the basis of issuance of invoice (per Notification No. 66/2017 CT), this provision is practically of limited relevance for supply of goods.

question_html: A machine is to be supplied and installed at the buyer's site. Purchase order with an advance of Rs. 80,000 is received on 10th July for a machine worth Rs. 18,00,000, and the entry is duly made in the seller's books. The machine is assembled, tested at site, and accepted by the buyer on 25th August. Invoice is raised on 28th August. Balance payment of Rs. 17,20,000 is received on 5th September. What is the time of supply for the purpose of payment of tax?

options.A: 25th August, being the date on which the goods were made available to the recipient as per section 31(1)(b), which is the date by which the invoice should have been issued [Section 12(2)(a)]
options.B: 10th July, being the date on which the advance payment was received and duly recorded
options.C: 28th August, being the actual date on which the invoice was raised by the supplier

Since the machine is installed and made available to the recipient (via assembly/testing/acceptance) on 25th August, the invoice should have been issued by this date under section 31(1)(b). Therefore, the time of supply for the entire amount of Rs. 18,00,000 is 25th August.

Since the invoice has not been issued, the time of supply for payment of tax will be the last date on which the invoice was required to be issued. question_html: Ganesh Traders sold goods to Vinayak Stores on 10th July, with a condition that interest at 2% per month would be charged if Vinayak Stores failed to pay within 15 days of delivery. What is the time of supply for the goods and for the addition in value by way of interest respectively?

options.A: 10th July for the goods (the date of issue of invoice), and 12th August for the addition in value by way of interest (the date on which such addition in value is received)

subject: Goods and Services Tax
question_html: Determine the time of supply from the following: booking of a banquet hall on 12th February, sum agreed Rs. 40,000, with an advance of Rs. 8,000 received on the same date; the function is held in the banquet hall on 5th June; tax invoice is issued on 30th July for Rs. 40,000, indicating a balance of Rs. 32,000 payable; the balance payment of Rs. 32,000 is received on 10th August. What is the time of supply of the service?

options.A: 30th July for the entire Rs. 40,000, being the date on which the tax invoice was actually issued
options.B: 12th February for Rs. 8,000 (the date of payment of the advance, earlier than the date of provision of service) and 5th June for the balance Rs. 32,000 (the date of provision of service, since the invoice was not issued within the prescribed time limit)
options.C: 5th June for the entire Rs. 40,000, being the date on which the function was held in the banquet hall
options.D: 12th February for the entire Rs. 40,000, being the date on which the booking was originally made

answer_html:
Correct answer: (B) 12th February for Rs. 8,000 (the date of payment of the advance, earlier than the date of provision of service) and 5th June for the balance Rs. 32,000 (the date of provision of service, since the invoice was not issued within the prescribed time limit)

As per Rule 47, the tax invoice is to be issued within 30 days of supply of service. Here, the invoice (30th July) is not issued within the prescribed time limit (i.e. within 30 days from 5th June). As per section 13(2)(b), the time of supply is the date of provision of service or date of receipt of payment, whichever is earlier. For the advance of Rs. 8,000, the date of payment (12th February) is earlier than the date of provision of service (5th June), so the time of supply for that amount is 12th February. For the balance Rs. 32,000, the time of supply is 5th June, the date of provision of service.

options.B: The due date for filing the periodical GST return of Prakhar Facility Services for the relevant tax period, applying the residual rule of section 13(5) directly
options.C: 22nd March, the date on which the Residents' Welfare Association (the recipient) records the receipt of service in its books of account, since clauses (a) and (b) of section 13(2) cannot be applied for want of an invoice, ascertainable provision date, or the supplier's own record of payment receipt

What is the time of supply, assuming the invoice was issued within the prescribed time period?

options.A: 2nd August, being the date on which Kalash Infra Ltd. issued the cheque and recorded the payment in its own books of account
options.B: 3rd August, being the date on which the payment was debited from Kalash Infra Ltd.'s bank account
options.C: 5th August, being the date on which the payment was recorded in Netra Enterprises' own books of account
options.D: 14th July, being the earlier of the date of issue of invoice (14th July) and the date of receipt of payment by the supplier - which, per Explanation 2 to section 13(2), is the earlier of the date payment is credited to the supplier's bank account (4th August) or entered in the supplier's books (5th August), i.e. 4th August

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) 14th July, being the earlier of the date of issue of invoice (14th July) and the date of receipt of payment by the supplier - which, per Explanation 2 to section 13(2), is the earlier of the date payment is credited to the supplier's bank account (4th August) or entered in the supplier's books (5th August), i.e. 4th August

Comparing the invoice date (14th July) with the date of receipt of payment (4th August), the earlier date is 14th July, which is the time of supply.

question_html: Where a service is taxable under reverse charge and the invoice in respect of such service is required to be issued BY THE RECIPIENT (rather than by the supplier), the time of supply under section 13(3) shall be the earlier of:

question_html: Which of the following correctly captures the key distinction between the time of supply of goods and services under FORWARD CHARGE, insofar as advances are concerned?

case_facts_html: Meridian Steel Traders agreed to supply steel rods worth Rs. 6,00,000 to Okhla Fabricators on 4th April. In a separate transaction, Meridian Steel Traders agreed to supply aluminium sheets worth Rs. 3,00,000 to Okhla Fabricators on 10th May, and received an advance of Rs. 1,00,000 on the same day. The sheets were removed from the factory on 11th May, with the invoice issued on 13th May. The balance payment of Rs. 2,00,000 was made by Okhla Fabricators on 30th May. In a third, unrelated instance, Meridian Steel Traders dispatched a consignment of iron beams worth Rs. 2,50,000 to Okhla Fabricators on 15th June, but due to an internal oversight, no invoice was raised and the dispatch was not entered in the books of account; there is no evidence of any payment having been received.
question_html: What is the time of supply of the steel rods, for the purpose of payment of tax?

options.A: 7th April, being the actual date on which Meridian Steel Traders issued the invoice
options.B: 22nd April, being the date on which Okhla Fabricators paid the full consideration
options.C: 7th April, being the last date on which the invoice was required to be issued (i.e. on or before the date of removal, 5th April) is actually 5th April - however, since the invoice was in fact issued on 7th April which is later than the required date, the time of supply is the earlier statutory last date, i.e. 5th April
options.D: 4th April, being the date on which the contract for supply of steel rods was originally agreed

answer_html:

case_facts_html: Highland Timber Co. procures raw timber taxable under reverse charge from various unregistered dealers. In Transaction 1, the supplier issues an invoice on 6th March (30 days from this date elapse on 5th April); Highland Timber Co. receives the timber on 15th March, and makes payment on 2nd April. In Transaction 2, the supplier issues an invoice on 6th March (30 days elapse on 5th April); Highland Timber Co. receives the timber on 20th April (the consignment having been delayed due to a landslide blocking the highway), and makes payment on 10th May. In Transaction 3, Highland Timber Co. receives a consignment of timber from an unregistered dealer, but the dealer never issues any invoice or document in lieu thereof, and Highland Timber Co. itself fails to record either the receipt of goods or any payment in its books of account for several months.
question_html: What is the time of supply of the timber in Transaction 3?

options.A: The date on which the unregistered dealer would ordinarily have been expected to issue an invoice, notwithstanding that no invoice was actually issued
options.B: The due date for filing Highland Timber Co.'s periodical GST return, applying the general residual rule of section 12(5) directly in preference to section 12(3)
options.C: No GST liability arises at all in respect of Transaction 3, since none of the three parameters under section 12(3) could ever be satisfied
options.D: The date of entry of the timber in the books of account of Highland Timber Co. (the recipient), once such entry is eventually made, since none of the three parameters under section 12(3)(a), (b) or (c) can be ascertained

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) The date of entry of the timber in the books of account of Highland Timber Co. (the recipient), once such entry is eventually made, since none of the three parameters under section 12(3)(a), (b) or (c) can be ascertained

As per the proviso to section 12(3), where it is not possible to determine the time of supply under clause (a) (receipt of goods - undated in the books), (b) (payment - not recorded), or (c) (31st day from invoice - no invoice issued), the time of supply shall be the date of entry in the books of account of the recipient of supply. This residual rule within section 12(3) applies to Transaction 3.

case_facts_html: Zenith Consulting LLP provides strategic advisory services to Apex Builders Ltd. In Engagement 1, provision of service is completed on 8th January, and the invoice is issued on 2nd February (within 30 days of completion); payment is received on 28th February. question_html: What is the time of supply of the service in Engagement 1?

options.A: 2nd February, being the date of issue of invoice (issued within 30 days of the date of supply of service), since it is earlier than the date of receipt of payment (28th February)
options.B: 8th January, being the date on which the provision of the advisory service was actually completed
options.C: 28th February, being the date on which Zenith Consulting LLP received payment for Engagement 1
options.D: 3rd February, being the last date within 30 days from 8th January on which the invoice could have been issued

answer_html:
Correct answer: (A) 2nd February, being the date of issue of invoice (issued within 30 days of the date of supply of service), since it is earlier than the date of receipt of payment (28th February)

case_facts_html: Crescent Logistics Pvt. Ltd. avails various services taxable under reverse charge. In Scenario 1, a firm of advocates issues an invoice for legal services on 5th February; Crescent Logistics Pvt. Ltd. makes payment on 20th March, entered in its books on that date and debited from its bank account two days later. In Scenario 2, Crescent Logistics Pvt. Ltd. itself (as recipient) since the GTA is unregistered; payment is made on 25th February, entered in the books on that date and debited from the bank account on 27th February, while Crescent Logistics Pvt. Ltd. issues its own invoice on 18th March. In Scenario 3, Crescent Logistics Pvt. Ltd. receives sponsorship services from a recognised sports body on which tax is payable under reverse charge; the supplier issues an invoice on 10th April, and there is a prolonged dispute over the amount payable, with payment finally being made on 25th August.
question_html: What is the time of supply of the legal services in Scenario 1?

options.A: 5th February, being the date on which the firm of advocates originally issued the invoice for legal services
options.B: 22nd March, being the date on which the payment was actually debited from Crescent Logistics Pvt. Ltd.'s bank account
options.C: 7th April, being the date immediately following 60 days from the date of issue of invoice
options.D: 20th March, being the date of payment (earlier of entry in books on 20th March or bank debit on 22nd March), since it is earlier than 7th April, the date immediately following 60 days from the date of issue of invoice

answer_html:
Correct answer: (D) 20th March, being the date of payment (earlier of entry in books on 20th March or bank debit on 22nd March), since it is earlier than 7th April, the date immediately following 60 days from the date of issue of invoice

As per section 13(3), the time of supply is the earlier of: date of payment (earlier of 20th March/22nd March, i.e. 20th March) and the date immediately following 60 days from the invoice (60 days from 5th February elapse on 6th April, so the date immediately following is 7th April). The earlier of 20th March and 7th April is 20th March, which is therefore the time of supply.

case_facts_html: Aqualine Water Solutions supplies purified water through a dedicated pipeline to Coastal Beverages Ltd. under a continuous supply contract running for two years, with monthly payments due as per the contract. Payments of Rs. 4 lakh each are made on the 8th of January, February and March, and invoices are issued by Aqualine Water Solutions on the same respective dates as the corresponding monthly payments in each of these three months. In a separate month, April, the monthly payment of Rs. 4 lakh is made by Coastal Beverages Ltd. on 8th April as usual, but Aqualine Water Solutions, due to an administrative delay, issues the invoice for the April supply only on 15th May.
question_html: What is the time of supply of the water supplied in January, February and March respectively?

options.A: Only 8th January, with the entire two-year contract value attributed to that single date since it is a continuous supply
options.B: The last day of the two-year contract period, since continuous supplies of goods are aggregated and taxed only upon completion of the full term
options.C: 8th January, 8th February and 8th March respectively, for goods valued at Rs. 4 lakh each, since the invoices are issued on or before each date on which the corresponding monthly payment is received, in accordance with section 31(4)
options.D: The due date for filing the periodical GST return for each respective month, treating continuous supply of goods as a residual case under section 12(5)

answer_html:
Correct answer: (C) 8th January, 8th February and 8th March respectively, for goods valued at Rs. 4 lakh each, since the invoices are issued on or before each date on which the corresponding monthly payment is received, in accordance with section 31(4)

As per section 31(4), in case of continuous supply of goods where successive statements of accounts or successive payments are involved, the invoice is to be issued before or at the time each such statement is issued or payment is received. Since invoices are issued on the same dates as the respective monthly payments (8th January, 8th February, 8th March), the time of supply for payment of tax is 8th January, 8th February and 8th March respectively, for goods valued at Rs. 4 lakh each.
